headline: Singapore’s S$3 Billion Laundering Case Ends With Nine Elite Banks Splitting a $21.5 Million Bill
deck: Singapore fined Credit Suisse, UOB, UBS, Citi, Julius Baer, LGT and three peers S$27.45 million for anti-laundering lapses — 0.915% of the assets police seized in the Fujian case.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Nine financial institutions fined S$27.45M (~$21.5M) combined for AML/CFT lapses — 0.915% of the S$3.0B+ in assets police seized or froze in the case, which drew formal FATF criticism.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: A corner money-changer waving through $1,800 in suspect cash and receiving a 0.915% civil bill
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: At Singapore’s institutional bank rate, the penalty would be $16.47 and zero jail time

sources.title: MAS Takes Regulatory Actions Against 9 Financial Institutions for AML-Related Breaches (S$27.45 Million)

interactive_art_spec.caption: Marina Bay in Singapore. Nine banks paid a combined S$27.45 million in a laundering case in which police seized or froze more than S$3 billion in assets.
